title: Where does 85 + (-60) land on a line with only zero?
description: A line that shows only zero is used to add negative sixty to eighty five. The number eighty five is drawn to the right of zero and an arrow of sixty steps goes back to the left. Keeko's doubt is that adding makes the number bigger.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding a negative number moves to the left on the unmarked number line, so the result is smaller than the start. Watch for students who add the sixty to the eighty five because the sign is plus.

source: The unmarked number line (UNL) shows the addition problem 85 + (-60) = ?
video_script.why: The child learns to add a negative number to a large number on an unmarked number line with only zero and the numbers needed, by moving left.
video_script.substitution: The book's own unmarked number line for 85 + (-60).
video_script.anchor: the unmarked number line of the book, with only zero marked at first
video_script.wrong_answer: the answer is one hundred forty five
video_script.wrong_move: adds sixty to eighty five because adding is meant to make a number bigger, and ignores that sixty is negative
video_script.payoff_line: Eighty five plus negative sixty lands on twenty five.

final_answer.spoken: eighty five plus negative sixty lands on twenty five

maths_rules: the unmarked number line (UNL) shows only the position of 0
85 is drawn to the right of 0; adding -60 is a move of 60 to the left
60 is less than 85, so the arrow stops to the right of 0
slip: 85 + 60 = 145 would move right, but the number added is negative
video_script.design: A line with only zero marked; eighty five is marked on it and an arrow of sixty steps runs back to the left.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a line with only 0 marked; the sum 85 + (-60) = ?

marks.scene: the title card arrives and a line with only 0 marked is drawn
marks.ask: the sum 85 + (-60) = ? is written above the line

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about adding on a line that shows only zero.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is eighty five plus negative sixty?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a line with only 0 marked; right = forward, left = backward

marks.line: the line with only 0 marked is highlighted and named
marks.dir: arrows mark right as forward and left as backward

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A line that shows only zero is called an unmarked number line.
We mark the other numbers on it as we need them.
<bookmark mark='dir'/>On it, to the right is forward, and to the left is backward.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eighty five plus negative sixty.

beats.on_screen: To find: where the move ends

marks.find: the words where the move ends are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find where the move ends.

beats.on_screen: mark 85 to the right of 0 on the line

marks.mark: the number 85 is marked far to the right of 0

narration: <bookmark mark='mark'/>Step one, mark eighty five to the right of zero. This is where the move starts.

beats.on_screen: an arrow of 60 steps goes left from 85

marks.arrow: an arrow of 60 steps runs left from 85, labelled -60

narration: <bookmark mark='arrow'/>Step two, adding negative sixty is a move of sixty steps backward.
Draw an arrow of that length from eighty five, towards the left.

beats.on_screen: the arrow of 60 is shorter than the distance 85 from 0, so it ends to the right of 0

marks.short: the arrow is compared with the distance from 0 to 85 and is seen to stop before 0
marks.end: the end of the arrow is circled to the right of 0

narration: <bookmark mark='short'/>Step three, sixty is less than eighty five, so the arrow stops before zero.
<bookmark mark='end'/>It ends to the right of zero.

marks.ans: the end of the arrow is labelled 25 and the sum is boxed
marks.pay: the sentence is written under the sum

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The arrow ends at twenty five.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Eighty five plus negative sixty lands on twenty five.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 85 + 60 = 145 shown far to the right of 85; struck out; the arrow back to 25 lights up

marks.doubt: 85 + 60 = 145 is written and an arrow runs right
marks.fix: the arrow is struck out and the sign -60 lights up
marks.why: the arrow runs back to the left of 85

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is one hundred forty five, because adding makes a number bigger.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the number being added is negative sixty.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Adding a negative number is a move backward, so the arrow goes left.
